intro: CIA cryptonyms, aliases and the agency paper trail on Oswald before the assassination, from the syllabus appendices II and III (pp. 83–86). In released CIA records a two-letter prefix (digraph) marks the subject area: AM for Cuba, KU for the CIA itself, OD for other U.S. agencies, PB for countries, ZR for Staff D projects. Where the syllabus gives only a surname, the full name is filled in from the cast of characters.

cryptonyms.meaning: "Tumbleweed," a German national (Gunter Schulz) recruited by the Soviets and doubled against them; reported on the KGB's Valeriy Kostikov in Mexico City.
Digraph for Cuban operations, organizations and individuals.

Tad Szulc of the New York Times.
Al Burt of the Miami Herald.
Don Bohning of the Miami Herald.
Paramilitary section of the DRE (AM/SPELL); its CIA contact was David Morales as "Dr. Menza."
Rolando Cubela Secades, the Cuban official the CIA courted in 1963 to kill Castro.
Listed without a description; in released records, the 1963 program backing Manuel Artime's force in Central America.
CIA domestic intelligence activities in the United States.
The Cuba project and invasion brigade (Bay of Pigs).
The 1961–62 Cuba project under Edward Lansdale and William Harvey.
Sensitivity indicator marking a secret operational message.
Special Group (Augmented), the high-level committee overseeing Mongoose.
The "Executive Action" assassination capability, run by William Harvey.

documents_intro: The syllabus argues the record shows FBI Director Hoover held significant information on Oswald (his Mexico City contact with the KGB's Valeriy Kostikov, suspected of belonging to the KGB department for sabotage and assassination) weeks before November 22, without ordering special surveillance, and that little of it came up in his calls with Johnson on November 22–23. Many records remain unreleased.

documents.from: FBI New Orleans (special agent in charge)
documents.summary: A message to the Director about Oswald, known only from a later reference.
Oswald's visits to the Soviet Embassy.
Oswald's Soviet Embassy contacts; identifies Kostikov and asks for background.

documents.to: Director, copied to Mexico City, New Orleans and Little Rock
documents.summary: A postal informant reports Oswald's brother Robert moved from Fort Worth; also relays the INS report of Oswald's Soviet contact in Mexico City.

Oswald's intercepted letter to the Soviet Embassy in Washington, mentioning plans to travel to Cuba and a meeting with "Kostin" (Kostikov); notes the status of the Oswald case is unknown to Washington because Dallas is the office of origin.
Reviews a CIA memo verifying the Kostikov contacts, Tumbleweed, and the absence of photos of the visit; backs off an absolute link between Kostikov and the KGB.
Lists urgent steps in Mexico to check whether Cubans, Soviets or others were connected to the assassination.
Anticipates the Warren Commission's questions and advises on the CIA's answers.
